newsitem.title: UK: UK ends Siemens-Plessey defence deal.
newsitem.headline: UK ends Siemens-Plessey defence deal.

text.p: Britain's Ministry of Defence has decided to terminate its contract with Siemens Plessey Systems for an automated electronic warfare system, defence producement minister James Arbuthnot said on Monday.
He said tests carried out in 1995 and last year had shown that the company's Vixen system had "operational shortcomings".

Arbuthnot said the ministry was now considering its legal position and would, if appropriate, pursue a claim for compensation. He said the cost so far of the Vixen project had been 50 million pounds ($80.2 million).
"The decision to cancel Vixen was taken only after careful consideration of the operational, contractual, financial and industrial implications," he said.

Arbuthnot said in a written parliamentary answer that various technical problems had delayed the Vixen project by several years. There was little prospect of these being overcome without further significant delay and expense. ($1=.6237 Pound)
